name: Shopify
description: Shopify sells the software that lets merchants run an online and in-store shop, and it earns far more from the money flowing through those shops than from the software itself. In 2025, 76 percent of revenue was merchant solutions, chiefly payment-processing and currency-conversion fees on Shopify Payments (65.6 percent of the $378 billion of sales on the platform), plus lending, shipping labels, POS hardware, ads and partner referral fees. The other 24 percent is subscriptions, typically one-month plans that renew automatically, with Plus and enterprise plans on annual or multi-year terms. Its payment processing rides on agreements with Stripe and PayPal, and most of its platform operations run on Google Cloud.

hq.note: Cover page of the FY2025 10-K lists Ottawa, Ontario and New York; remote-first company. Incorporated under the Canada Business Corporations Act.

businessLines.name: Merchant solutions
businessLines.how: Takes a per-transaction fee on the money merchants collect through Shopify Payments, plus interest and fees on merchant lending and smaller charges on shipping, hardware and advertising; revenue moves with merchant sales volume (GMV), not with merchant count.
businessLines.description: Shopify Payments (processing and currency-conversion fees), lending, shipping labels, POS hardware, App Store and Shop Campaigns advertising, partner referral fees.

businessLines.name: Subscription solutions
businessLines.how: Merchants pay a recurring fee, usually monthly with automatic renewal; Plus and enterprise merchants sign annual or multi-year terms, and the majority of GMV comes from those plans.
businessLines.description: Monthly or annual subscriptions to the platform (Basic, Grow, Advanced, Plus, enterprise), POS Pro per location, app sales, domain registration, themes, and variable platform fees.

brands.name: Shopify Plus
brands.note: Majority of GMV comes from Plus and enterprise merchants; share not quantified
